transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. For the past few years I feel worn out all the time, like I’m running on empty even when I’m not doing that much. I'm just hoping to get some help figuring out why I feel so constantly drained.
Beyond feeling physically drained, have you also experienced a persistent sense of sadness, hopelessness, or a loss of interest in the things you used to enjoy over these past few years?

Yes, deeply. Ever since my company restructured a little over three years ago, I've lived under this low, heavy, gray cloud that makes everything feel joyless, and I've lost all interest in things I used to love like painting, hiking, and photography. I also catch myself feeling hopeless, like this is just how my life is going to be now and nothing is ever going to change it.
During these past three years, have there been any periods of a few months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has this low mood been present almost every single day?

No, I haven't had any breaks from it at all; it has been completely steady over these last three years. Even when we took vacations or trips abroad, I just couldn't shake this gray feeling and never felt like my normal self.
Have you noticed any consistent changes in your appetite or sleep patterns—such as sleeping too much or too little, or eating significantly more or less—since this low mood began?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite. As for my sleep, I generally get a full night of sleep, but I still wake up feeling completely drained and exhausted rather than having trouble falling asleep or sleeping too much.
Have you experienced persistent feelings of low self-esteem, difficulty concentrating, or a sense of indecisiveness during these past three years?

Yes, I have definitely struggled with concentration and focus, to the point where I'm making small errors in my reports and taking days to finish tasks that used to take an afternoon. This has caused my work reviews to slip and left me really worried about my performance, though low self-esteem or indecisiveness haven't stood out as much as this constant brain fog.
Have you experienced any persistent feelings of hopelessness or a sense of being inadequate, such as feeling like a failure, during this time?

Yes, the hopelessness is really heavy. I constantly catch myself thinking that this flat, tired state is just how my life is going to be from now on. I've truly come to believe that no vacation, job change, or medication is ever going to make a difference.

Have you experienced any specific periods over these past three years where your symptoms became significantly more severe, such as feeling much worse for two weeks or longer, compared to your usual baseline of feeling 'gray' and drained?

No, I haven't really had any periods where my symptoms suddenly spiked or became much worse for a couple of weeks. This low, gray, and drained feeling has just been very steady and constant. It has basically become my new baseline ever since the restructuring three years ago.
